rows.why: S1 covers the header row, the BOM, row order and line endings, so items 4, 2 and 5 also apply. Item 1 is the closest because the scenario is mainly about the header and its exact columns. Its pick writes exactly 'Requisition ID,Title,Status,Openings,Filled,Created'. The other three picks also match: a U+FEFF prefix, sorting by createdAt then id, and CRLF on every row including the last.

S2 expects readable status labels ('Open', 'On hold', ...), but item 9's pick writes the raw value such as 'on_hold'. Item 8 also applies and also disagrees: it writes the full ISO timestamp with milliseconds, not 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Only item 7, an empty cell for a missing title, matches its part.
Item 3 asks what an empty list produces. Its pick returns the BOM and the header row only, which is what S3 expects.

Item 6 asks when a cell is quoted. Its pick quotes only for a comma, a double quote, CR or LF. S4 also requires quoting a title that starts or ends with a space, and the pick would leave that unquoted.
No item asks about defusing titles that start like a formula (a leading '=', '+', '-', '@', tab or CR). Item 6 only covers when to quote and escape, which is a different behaviour.

Item 10 asks what happens with an unknown status, invalid counts, filled > openings or an invalid date. Its pick throws an Error naming the requisition id, as S6 expects. Item 11's pick also matches S6's limits: counts that are whole numbers of at least 0 are accepted.
